Done. Typecheck clean, build clean, 46 new tests passing, no new failures (the 29 failures are pre-existing on a clean tree — a `TOOL_REGISTRATION_ORDER` circular-init bug in `browser-tools.ts`, unrelated to this work).

## What changed

**Live is no longer a parallel page.** The conversation is owned by the chat panel and appears as a full-screen surface over it. `/live` is now a pre-flight room — check your key, pick a model, choose whether camera/screen start on — and "Start talking" fires the same code path as the composer button. One implementation, in `components/live/`:

- `use-live-session.ts` — the whole runtime. The connection is disposable, the conversation is not: retrying or switching model tears down the socket and keeps the transcript, the camera, and your mute state.
- `LiveConversation.tsx` — phone-call layout. Big subject, one row of round controls, transcript present but not the main event. The old telemetry HUD (frames sent, tier labels, tool ledger) is gone.

**Camera actually works now.**
- Screen sharing was silently dropping every frame — the frame sampler skipped on `document.hidden`, and sharing a screen means looking at another window. Screen capture is now exempt (de-duplication still applies, so a static window doesn't stream).
- Camera and screen can be turned on and off *mid-conversation*. Both providers gained `setVideo()`; previously vision was fixed at connect time, so "look at this" meant reconnecting.
- Front/rear camera flip, device selection with a fallback when a remembered camera vanishes, `facingMode: ideal` so a single-webcam desktop doesn't fail outright, and an `onEnded` hook so the browser's own "stop sharing" bar updates the UI.
- Mute is real mute (`setMicrophoneMuted`), not a disconnect.

**Errors became actions.** `live-errors.ts` classifies every failure once into a kind plus recovery flags; the UI renders buttons from the flags. A 404 now reads "Gemini 3.1 Flash Live is not available on this key" with a one-click switch to the next model, rather than "Realtime session mint failed (404)". Camera failures are always non-fatal — voice continues, a dismissible notice explains.

**Models are curated.** `live-models.ts` grades each model and defines the fallback chain, so "try another model" walks down a real list instead of bouncing.

**Visual states.** `LiveVisualizer` draws on canvas from one rAF loop — never React state. Four distinguishable states: connecting (dim breath), listening (rings driven by your *actual* mic level via an analyser, so you can see you're being heard), speaking (outward travelling wave), working (orbiting segment — a session fetching something previously looked identical to a dead one). Honours `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**Composer, per your screenshot.** Dictation and live are now two buttons, not one whose meaning depends on a hidden setting: mic puts text in the composer to edit, the filled waveform button opens the conversation. A `+` menu absorbed attach/model/reasoning. The model selector moved to the top-left of the chat header.

Two notes:
- The round control buttons were being squashed by a global `[role="dialog"] button { width: auto !important }` — `dialog-compact-button` reinforces it rather than escaping it. They're sized with matching min/max width instead, which that rule can't touch.
- I couldn't screenshot to verify visually (the Chrome extension isn't connected), so the layout is confirmed by build and module transforms only, not by eye. Dev server's up at `localhost:3000` if you want to look.
